title: The Place the Prophet ﷺ Told You Never to Enter
_accuracy: All sourced: the Prophet ﷺ passing Al-Hijr on the way to Tabuk and forbidding entry except while weeping (Sahih al-Bukhari 3379); Al-Hijr named in Qur'an 15:80; Thamud carving mountain homes (7:74); the she-camel sign (7:73, 26:155); killing it and the ṣayḥah/scream after three days (11:65–67, 54:31). Map is real Esri satellite imagery pinned to Hegra/Mada'in Salih (26.7917°N, 37.9539°E). No human depictions.

beats.say: There's a place in Saudi Arabia the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, warned his companions not to enter. And to hurry through it, covering their faces.
He told them not to drink from its wells. And not to enter, unless they were weeping.
Because this is Al-Hijr. The land of Thamud.
Right here. In the deserts of Al-Ula.
The Quran even names them. The companions of Al-Hijr, who denied the messengers.
Thamud were master builders. They carved entire homes into solid mountains.
So Allah sent them the prophet Salih, with one miracle. A she-camel. And one rule. Let it drink freely, and never harm it.
They killed it anyway. Three days later, a single scream from the sky ended them all.
Their homes still stand today. Empty. So the Prophet rushed past, and warned: don't enter, unless you're weeping. Follow, for the places history tried to bury.

sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 3379 — the Prophet ﷺ at al-Hijr: do not enter upon those punished except while weeping; he covered his head and hurried through the valley.
Qur'an 15:80–84 — the companions of al-Hijr denied the messengers.
Qur'an 7:73–79; 11:61–68; 26:141–158; 54:23–31 — Thamud, Salih, the she-camel, and the ṣayḥah (scream).
